tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HodgeStructures.summary: Mathlib has no Hodge theory, but Tau Ceti's TauCeti/Geometry/Hodge (about 11,000 lines, sorry-free) already proves essentially the whole roadmap: pure Hodge structures with Deligne's decomposition equivalence, morphisms, duals, tensor products, internal Hom, Tate twists and the weight-one complex-structure bridge (L0); polarizations, the Weil operator, the positive-definite Hodge form and semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures as orthogonal complements and a decomposition into simple substructures (L1); mixed Hodge structures with Deligne's bigrading, its fine conjugation relation, functoriality and strictness for both filtrations (L2); and Hodge types, period-domain points, the Hodge-number partition and the isometry group of a bilinear form (L3). What is genuinely missing is small: the abelian-category structure on mixed Hodge structures (kernels, images and cokernels as objects), a bundled category in which semisimplicity is stated categorically, and a general constructor of integral weight-one structures from a lattice with a complex structure and Riemann form beyond the standard rank-two example.

targets.target: Pure Hodge structure of weight n: a bounded n-opposed decreasing filtration, stated once over a complex space with a conjugation and specialized to an integral lattice via IsBaseChange
targets.note: The conjugation-parametric object and the integral abbreviation over an abstract base change are exactly the README's design; separatedness F_bot is derived rather than a field, and freeness/finiteness of the lattice is imposed only where used (so slightly more general).

targets.target: Hodge components piece p = F^p ⊓ conj F^(n-p)
targets.note: Defined as F p ⊓ conjF (n - p), exactly as stated.

targets.target: Milestone: the Hodge components form an internal direct sum (DirectSum.IsInternal hs.piece), via F^p = ⨆_{p'≥p} H^{p'} and independence
targets.note: Proved with no finiteness hypothesis; decompositionEquiv also gives the converse (Deligne's equivalence between opposed filtrations and conjugation-symmetric bounded decompositions).

targets.target: Morphisms of pure Hodge structures (preserving the filtration and hence every Hodge component)
targets.note: Integral morphisms with derived complex action, identity, composition and additive group structure; the lattice-free predicate IsMorphism is also provided. There is no Category instance for pure Hodge structures.

targets.target: Hodge symmetry of components: conj (piece p) = piece (n - p)
targets.note: Stated as (hs.piece p).map conj = hs.piece (n - p).

targets.target: Tensor product, internal Hom and dual of pure Hodge structures
targets.note: Weights n₁ + n₂, n₂ - n₁ and -n respectively; the internal Hom needs no finiteness hypothesis and is compared with V^* ⊗ W over a finite-dimensional source.

targets.target: Tate structure ℤ(m) and Tate twist V(m) with weight n - 2m and F^p(V(m)) = F^(p+m) V
targets.note: The twist is defined as the shifted filtration on the same space (the canonical presentation of V ⊗ ℤ(m)), with the weight and shift pinned as in the README; no lemma compares it with tensorProduct V (tate m).

targets.target: Effectivity HodgeStructure.IsEffective (F^0 = ⊤, equivalently F^(n+1) = ⊥)
targets.note: Defined as F 0 = ⊤ with the equivalence to F (n + 1) = ⊥ and vanishing of components outside [0, n] proved.

targets.target: Weight-one instance bridge: real form V_ℝ with its structure map, the complex structure J of an effective weight-one structure, identification of its ±i-eigenspaces with H^(1,0), H^(0,1), and the converse construction from J
targets.note: J is the Weil operator restricted to the real points (for any odd weight); the eigenspace comparison assumes effectivity, and the converse builds an effective weight-one structure on ℂ ⊗_ℝ V whose Weil operator is J. Only the standard rank-two lattice example (StandardWeightOne) is packaged as an integral instance from a lattice with J and a Riemann form.

duplicates.note: A5's equivalence between polarized complex tori and polarizable integral Hodge structures of types (-1,0),(0,-1) contains the linear-algebraic weight-one bridge (lattice with complex structure ↔ effective weight-one Hodge structure) that this layer states and Tau Ceti already has.

targets.target: IsPolarization (Hodge–Riemann relations as a Prop on a fixed integral form), Polarization (form plus proof, with derived complex form Q) and IsPolarizable
targets.note: (-1)^n-symmetry, nondegeneracy, orthogonality of F^p and F^(n+1-p) and positivity of i^(p-q) Q(x, conj x) on H^(p,q), with the sign convention pinned in the README.

targets.target: RationalHodgeSubstructure (a ℚ-subspace whose complexification is derived and spanned by its Hodge components)
targets.note: Carries only WQ; WC is derived by rationalToComplexSubmodule and conjugation stability is a lemma.

targets.target: Milestone: every rational Hodge substructure of a polarizable structure has a Q-orthogonal rational Hodge-substructure complement, complementary over ℚ and over ℂ
targets.note: Assumes Module.Finite ℚ Vℚ, as the milestone implicitly does.

targets.target: Semisimplicity of polarizable rational Hodge structures
targets.note: Stated object-wise: the lattice of rational Hodge substructures is complemented, and a polarizable structure is a finite independent sum of simple substructures. There is no bundled category of polarizable ℚ-Hodge structures, so the categorical phrasing is not stated; the layer's own milestone is the complement theorem.

targets.target: Weil operator C: definition from the pieces, action by i^(p-q), C² = (-1)^n, compatibility with conjugation and with Q
targets.note: All four properties the layer lists are proved; uniqueness of C and the odd-weight complex structure are also present.

targets.target: Hodge form h(u,v) = Q(Cu, conj v), positive-definite Hermitian on V_ℂ
targets.note: Tau Ceti uses h u v = Q(C(conj u), v), conjugate-linear in the first argument; hodgeForm_eq_conj relates it to the README's convention, and it is packaged as an inner-product core.

duplicates.note: A5's Riemann bilinear relations for polarized complex tori are the weight-one case of this layer's Hodge–Riemann polarization, already proved in Tau Ceti as isPolarization_of_weilOperator_invariant_on_realPoints_of_pos.

targets.target: MixedHodgeStructure: bounded rational weight filtration WQ, bounded Hodge filtration F, and graded_pure as a pure Hodge structure of weight k on each complexified gr^W_k
targets.note: graded_pure is an existential over HodgeStructure on the rational graded piece whose filtration is gradedF, equivalent to the README's Nonempty formulation; pure structures embed as mixed ones.

targets.target: Derived complex weight filtration WC with monotonicity and conjugation stability
targets.note: WC is an abbreviation for rationalToComplexSubmodule of WQ.

targets.target: Induced conjugation and filtration on graded pieces (gradedConj, gradedF) and the isomorphism WC_k/WC_(k-1) ≃ ℂ ⊗_ℚ gr^W_k
targets.note: The graded conjugation is packaged as a Conjugation, as the README requests.

targets.target: Milestone: strictness of morphisms of mixed Hodge structures for the rational and complexified weight filtrations and for the Hodge filtration
targets.note: Exactly range f ⊓ W'_k = f(W_k) and range f_ℂ ⊓ F'^p = f_ℂ(F^p), proved through the Deligne bigrading.

targets.target: Deligne bigrading I^(p,q) defined by the closed formula, internal direct sum, recovery of F and of W_ℂ
targets.note: The bigrading is data, not an existential, as the README insists.

targets.target: Conjugation relation conj(I^(p,q)) ≡ I^(q,p) modulo ⨆_{r<q, s<p} I^(r,s)
targets.note: The fine lower-bidegree relation is proved (the coarser relation modulo W_(p+q-2) is also there); the 2026-09-01 status note describing only the coarse form is out of date.

targets.target: Functoriality: a morphism carries I^(p,q) into I^(p,q)
targets.note: Stated for morphisms given by a single rational map with derived complex action.

targets.target: Conjugation-equivariance of the complexified rational map on an abstract complex model, fC ∘ conj = conj ∘ fC
targets.note: Proved for arbitrary IsBaseChange models (by induction along the base-change witness), not only the concrete tensor product.

targets.target: Bundled morphisms and category of mixed Hodge structures with its abelian-category structure (kernels and cokernels are mixed Hodge structures)
targets.note: The category is preadditive and ℚ-linear with rational and complex realization functors, and kernels and images are sub-mixed Hodge structures as predicates; missing are kernel, image and cokernel as mixed Hodge structure objects and the Abelian instance.

targets.target: HodgeType: a weight, finitely supported Hodge numbers h : ℤ → ℕ and Hodge symmetry h p = h (weight - p)
targets.note: Every Hodge structure has a Hodge type (hodgeType), with symmetry proved from conj_piece.

targets.target: PeriodDomain.Point: a Hodge structure of prescribed type polarized by a fixed integral form
targets.note: The form enters through the IsPolarization field, not as duplicated data, as the layer specifies.

targets.target: Milestone: the Hodge numbers partition the dimension, ∑ᶠ p, h p = dim_ℂ V_ℂ = rank_ℤ V
targets.note: Both the complex-dimension and lattice-rank forms are proved.

targets.target: Symmetry group Aut(V, Qint) of integral automorphisms preserving the form, as a Subgroup
targets.note: Built for an arbitrary bilinear form over a commutative ring under the name isometryGroup rather than IsLatticeIsometry, with base change to ℂ as a group homomorphism and automatic invertibility of isometries of a nondegenerate lattice form.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge.summary: Tau Ceti already covers much of Layer A and parts of Layers B and E: invertible sheaves closed under tensor product, scheme Weil and Cartier divisors with the Weil–Cartier equivalence on Noetherian integral curves whose codimension-one local rings are DVRs, the sheaves O_X(D) with an injective additive map from divisor classes to line-bundle classes, the residue-weighted degree and an abstract Pic⁰; cohomology of O_X-modules with long exact and Mayer–Vietoris sequences; Riemann–Roch, genus, Weil-differential duality and deg K = 2g − 2 for algebraic function fields; and abelian varieties with Hom groups, products, base change, dimension, the tangent space at the identity and commutativity (from Mathlib's rigidity theorem). Genuinely missing are Pic X as a group (line bundles have no duals yet) and the other half of the divisor dictionary with deg L = χ(L) − χ(𝒪_X); affine acyclicity, finiteness, vanishing, Serre duality and Riemann–Roch for coherent cohomology of schemes, together with a bridge from function fields to curves; the whole relative theory of Layer C (higher direct images, base change, semicontinuity, formal functions, relative effective Cartier divisors, Symᵈ X); the Picard functor, rigidification and representability; dual abelian varieties, polarizations, the theorems of the cube and square and [n] as an isogeny for n ≠ ±1; and the Jacobian itself with the Abel–Jacobi morphism, its universal property and base change.

targets.target: Invertible sheaves (locally free rank-one O_X-modules) on a scheme, closed under tensor product
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines invertible sheaves on an arbitrary scheme as the full subcategory of X.Modules that are locally free of rank one (a site-level predicate), and proves closure under tensor product. Mathlib has only SheafOfModules.IsLocallyFree.

targets.target: Picard group Pic X: isomorphism classes of line bundles as a group under tensor product
targets.note: Tau Ceti's LineBundleClass X (iso classes of invertible sheaves) is only a commutative monoid under tensor product: duals/inverses of invertible sheaves are not constructed, so no group Pic X exists. Mathlib's CommRing.Pic is the Picard group of a ring (affine case) only.

targets.target: Weil divisors: finite formal Z-sums of codimension-one points of a scheme
targets.note: Defined for every scheme as WeilDivisor on the codimension-one points, and identified with Mathlib's AlgebraicCycle X Z restricted to finite support in codimension one; Mathlib alone has only algebraic cycles, no divisor API.

targets.target: Cartier divisors and principal divisors (Cartier and Weil)
targets.note: Cartier divisors are global sections of the sheaf quotient K_X^x/O_X^x, defined only for integral schemes (enough for curves); principal Weil divisors come from Mathlib's Scheme.ord assembled by OrderSystem.ofScheme on Noetherian integral schemes.

targets.target: Weil = Cartier on a smooth curve
targets.note: Additive equivalence for Noetherian integral schemes of dimension <= 1 whose codimension-one local rings are DVRs (hypotheses as instance plus hX : forall x, coheight x <= 1); a smooth connected curve satisfies these, but no lemma deriving them from smoothness was found.

targets.target: Cartier/Weil divisors to line bundles, D -> O_X(D), and Cl(X) = Pic X
targets.note: On Noetherian integral curves with DVR local rings, O_X(D) is invertible, O_X(D+E) = O_X(D) (x) O_X(E), and Cl(X) -> line-bundle classes is an injective additive map; surjectivity (every line bundle comes from a divisor), a direct Cartier-divisor-to-line-bundle map, and Cl(X) = Pic X are missing. Affine Dedekind case: classGroupAddEquiv with Mathlib's ClassGroup, and Mathlib's ClassGroup.equivPic.

targets.target: Divisor degree sum_x [kappa(x):k] ord_x
targets.note: relativeDegree f weights coefficients by residue degrees of f : X -> Y; applied to the structure morphism of a curve over k it is the divisor degree, and D - (deg D) x0 has degree zero at a rational point.

targets.target: deg L := chi(L) - chi(O_X) for line bundles, and agreement with the divisor degree
targets.note: Only a truncated alternating sum of cohomology dimensions and its conditional additivity exist; no degree of a line bundle via Euler characteristics and no comparison with sum_x [kappa(x):k] ord_x.

targets.target: Pic^0 X = ker deg as an abstract group
targets.note: picZero is the kernel of the weighted degree on a divisor class group, but it takes as a hypothesis that principal divisors have degree zero; that hypothesis is proved only for places of an algebraic function field (product formula), not for OrderSystem.ofScheme on a proper curve, and it is on divisor classes, not on Pic X of line bundles.

duplicates.note: Integration layer that states the same divisor and line-bundle targets (divisors, line bundles, Picard objects) and explicitly routes them through JacobianChallenge.

12A/12D plan orders of vanishing and degrees at closed points and Weil divisors on the regular model with principal divisors, degrees, linear equivalence and class groups, the scheme-side divisor targets of Layer A.
Function-field form of the same targets: divisors, residue-weighted degree, principal divisors with the product formula, and Cl^0(F) as the kernel of degree (abstract Pic^0).
States extending the invertible-sheaf API with tensor powers, Cartier divisors, pullback and degree on components (shared contracts J-A1/J-A2 for Pic X and deg L = chi(L) - chi(O)).
Function-field form of divisors, degree weighted by residue degrees, principal-divisor product formula and Pic^0, overlapping Layer A's divisor/degree/Pic^0 targets.

targets.target: Coherent (finitely presented) O_X-modules and their cohomology H^i(X,F), with long exact sequence and k-linear structure
targets.note: Mathlib has Ext-based cohomology of abelian sheaves on any site and SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation; Tau Ceti packages H^i(X,M) for every O_X-module (H^0 = global sections, long exact and Mayer-Vietoris sequences, Gamma(X,O_X)-module structure) and the category of finitely presented sheaves (coherent on locally Noetherian X).

targets.target: Acyclicity of affines: H^i(Spec A, quasi-coherent F) = 0 for i > 0
targets.note: Only acyclicity of flasque sheaves (hence skyscrapers) is proved; Serre vanishing for quasi-coherent sheaves on affine schemes is not, and Tau Ceti notes the missing comparison between H' on an open and cohomology of the restricted sheaf.

targets.target: Cech cohomology agrees with derived-functor cohomology on a separated scheme
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Cech complex of a presheaf for a family of objects, and Mayer-Vietoris for two opens is exact; no Cech-to-derived comparison theorem exists.

targets.target: Finite-dimensionality of H^i(X,F) for coherent F on proper X/k
targets.note: No finiteness theorem for coherent cohomology of proper schemes; the Tau Ceti Euler-characteristic results take finite-dimensionality as a hypothesis. Only the function-field analogues (L(D) and the repartition cokernel A_F/(A_F(D)+F) are finite-dimensional) exist.

targets.target: Vanishing above dimension (H^2 = 0 on a curve)
targets.note: Only conditional vanishing: if X is covered by two opens which, with their intersection, have no higher cohomology, then H^n = 0 for n >= 2. No Grothendieck vanishing and no unconditional H^2 = 0 for curves.

targets.target: Genus g := dim_k H^1(X, O_X)
targets.note: No scheme-level genus. The function-field genus (Stichtenoth: sup of deg D + 1 - l(D)) is proved to equal dim_k A_F/(A_F(0)+F), the adelic H^1(O), and the dimension of regular Weil differentials, for an algebraic function field with exact constant field; no bridge to curves as schemes.

targets.target: Riemann-Roch chi(L) = deg L + 1 - g
targets.note: Proved for divisors of an algebraic function field F/k with exact constant field: l(D) = deg D + 1 - g + l(W - D), with i(D) = dim_k A_F/(A_F(D)+F) (adelic H^1). Missing: the scheme/line-bundle statement via coherent cohomology and Euler characteristics, and the comparison of places with closed points of a curve.

targets.target: Serre duality with the relative dualizing sheaf omega_{X/k}: H^i(L) = H^{1-i}(omega (x) L^{-1})^*
targets.note: Function-field duality (Stichtenoth 1.5.14) is proved: L(W - D) = Omega_F(D), the Weil differentials, which are the dual of A_F/(A_F(D)+F). There is no dualizing sheaf or sheaf of differentials of a scheme (Mathlib has only a presheaf-of-modules relative differentials construction) and no scheme-level Serre duality.

targets.target: deg omega_{X/k} = 2g - 2
targets.note: Proved for the canonical divisor class of Weil differentials of a function field with exact constant field; nothing for the dualizing sheaf of a curve.

duplicates.note: States Riemann-Roch, Serre duality and genus for curves, routed through JacobianChallenge.

States finite-dimensionality of coherent cohomology on proper curves, vanishing above degree one, genus as dim H^1(O), and a relative dualizing sheaf that restricts to omega_{X/k} (shared contracts J-B and J-B/SR-2).
Function-field form of the same theorems: Riemann-Roch, the duality i(D) = l(W - D), deg W = 2g - 2 and g as the dimension of the adelic H^1 (already built in Tau Ceti).

targets.target: Pushforward (and higher direct images) of coherent sheaves along proper, flat, finitely presented morphisms, with coherence
targets.note: Only the underlying functors f_* and f^* on O-modules, their adjunction, and quasi-coherence of pushforwards along maps of affine schemes exist; no higher direct images R^i f_* and no coherence of proper pushforwards.

targets.target: Flat base change for (higher) pushforwards
targets.note: No base-change comparison map or flat base change theorem for cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves in either library.

targets.target: Cohomology and base change, semicontinuity, Grauert
targets.note: No semicontinuity of fibre cohomology dimensions, Grauert's theorem, or cohomology-and-base-change theorem.

targets.target: Theorem on formal functions
targets.note: No formal completion of schemes along closed subschemes and no theorem on formal functions.

targets.target: Relative effective Cartier divisors
targets.note: Only Mathlib's ideal sheaves/closed subschemes exist; no effective Cartier divisors (even absolute, as closed subschemes cut out locally by a nonzerodivisor) and no relative version flat over the base.

targets.target: Symmetric powers Sym^d X as schemes (smooth projective for a smooth curve)
targets.note: Tau Ceti only has the set-level model: effective degree-d formal divisors on a type of points are equivalent to Mathlib's Sym X d. No scheme Sym^d X, no quotients of schemes by finite groups, no smoothness/projectivity.

duplicates.note: States coherent proper pushforward and R^i f_*, cohomology and base change, Grauert and upper semicontinuity, and sections as effective Cartier divisors compatible with base change (shared contract J-C).
Plans proper-flat coherent cohomology and base change in higher relative dimension, extending the same Layer C theory beyond curves.
Develops relative effective Cartier divisors on smooth relative curves (fibre criterion, sections, sums, base change, degree), the Layer C relative-divisor target.
Plans the theorem on formal functions (and formal GAGA) in the proper finite-presentation setting, a stated Layer C target.

targets.target: Relative Picard functor Pic_{X/k}: fppf sheafification of T -> Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)
targets.note: Mathlib has the fppf topology on schemes and Tau Ceti has line-bundle classes on a single scheme (monoid only); there is no pullback-functorial Pic(X_T), no quotient by Pic(T), and no Picard sheaf.

targets.target: Picard stack vs Picard functor/sheaf vs rigidified functor, and the Brauer-type obstruction between Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) and Pic_{X/k}(T)
targets.note: Only the Brauer group of a field exists as an ingredient; none of the three Picard objects and no obstruction sequence.

targets.target: Rigidification along the section x0 and the Poincare bundle
targets.note: No line bundles trivialized along a section, no rigidified Picard functor, no Poincare bundle.

targets.target: Pic^0 as the degree-0 open-and-closed component / subfunctor of degree-0 line bundles on geometric fibres, with local constancy of degree in flat families
targets.note: Only the abstract group Pic^0 of divisor classes (Layer A) exists; no functorial Pic^0, no degree on fibres of flat families, no local constancy.

targets.target: Representability via symmetric powers: Abel maps AJ_d : Sym^d X -> Pic^d, D -> O_X(D - d x0), birational and surjective for d = g
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the set-level divisor-class shadow (D -> [D - deg D x0] in abstract Pic^0, fibres on Sym X d are complete linear systems, and for function fields every degree-0 class has an effective representative once the degree is >= g); Mathlib has Zariski-local representability of sheaves. No scheme morphism, no Sym^d X, no birationality, no representability of Pic^0.

targets.target: General Picard scheme of a projective variety via Hilbert/Quot schemes (Grothendieck), then specialize
targets.note: No Hilbert, Quot or Picard schemes in either library.

targets.target: Properness/projectivity of Pic^0
targets.note: Nothing, since Pic^0 is not constructed as a scheme.

duplicates.note: States Picard schemes and Jacobians for curves, routed through JacobianChallenge.
Constructs the relative degree-zero Picard functor (as an algebraic space) and the rigidified Poincare bundle, for abelian schemes rather than curves.
Plans relative degree-zero Picard representability criteria via algebraic spaces, overlapping the general Picard-scheme representability route of Layer D.

Constructs, for elliptic curves over a base, the fppf sheafified Picard functor of T -> Pic(E_T)/Pic(T), its zero-rigidified version, the degree-zero open-and-closed subfunctor, its representability and the normalized Poincare bundle.

targets.target: Abelian variety over k (smooth, proper, geometrically connected group scheme) with basic API and dim
targets.note: Bundled as a proper geometrically integral group scheme over Spec K (equivalent for group schemes over a field); smoothness and geometric connectedness are derived, and there are commutative Hom groups, End ring, finite products, zero object, base change along field extensions. dim is the topological Krull dimension; nothing computes it (e.g. dim = dim T_0 A).

targets.target: Commutativity is automatic (rigidity)
targets.note: Mathlib proves a proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative; Tau Ceti installs it as an instance on AbelianVariety.

targets.target: Tangent space at the identity of an abelian variety
targets.note: T_0 A is the Zariski tangent space at the identity as a finite-dimensional K-vector space, with dimension that of m/m^2; the regular-point formula dim T_x = coheight x exists for schemes, but it is not applied to abelian varieties.

targets.target: T_0 Pic^0 = H^1(X, O_X), hence dim Jac X = g
targets.note: No Pic^0 scheme, no identification of its tangent space with H^1(X,O_X), no scheme-level genus, and no dimension computation.

targets.target: Theorem of the cube / theorem of the square
targets.note: Not present in either library (no line bundles on products of abelian varieties, no seesaw).

targets.target: Dual abelian variety
targets.note: No dual abelian variety (needs Pic^0 of an abelian variety); Tau Ceti's Cartier duality is only for finite locally free commutative affine group schemes.

targets.target: Polarizations; the theta divisor gives Jac a principal polarization
targets.note: No polarizations, no phi_L : A -> A^dual, no theta divisor.

targets.target: [n] as an isogeny
targets.note: [n] is defined in End A and isogenies (finite surjective homomorphisms, no separability assumption) are defined with base change, but only [-1] is proved to be an isogeny; [n] for n != 0 is missing. For Weierstrass elliptic curves (function-field model, not AbelianVariety) [n] is an isogeny of degree n^2.

targets.target: Characteristic p: p-torsion non-etale, inseparable isogenies, no hidden perfect-field assumptions
targets.note: The AbelianVariety isogeny notion avoids separability and perfect-field assumptions, but nothing about p-torsion or inseparable isogenies of abelian varieties is proved; only for Weierstrass elliptic curves is [n] shown separable iff n != 0 in the base field.

duplicates.note: States rigidity and commutativity, the theorem of the square and cube, homomorphisms, products and base change for abelian schemes (more general base).
States the dual abelian scheme, Poincare bundle and polarizations phi_L, the Layer E dual/polarization targets over a general base.
States that [n] is finite locally free of rank n^(2g) and etale exactly when n is invertible, keeping p-primary torsion scheme-theoretic, overlapping Layer E's [n]-isogeny and characteristic-p items.

targets.target: Abel-Jacobi morphism aj : X -> Jac X with x0 -> 0 (the d = 1 Abel map)
targets.note: Only set-level shadows: a point x goes to the class of [x] - w(x)[x0] in the abstract Pic^0 of an order system (conditional on principal divisors having degree zero), and for Weierstrass curves the rational points are additively equivalent to degree-zero divisor classes of the function field via P -> (P) - (O). No Jacobian scheme and no morphism of schemes.

targets.target: Universal (Albanese) property: every pointed morphism (X,x0) -> (A,0) to an abelian variety factors uniquely through aj via a homomorphism Jac X -> A
targets.note: No Jacobian variety and no Albanese-type universal property in either library.

targets.target: Base-change compatibility of the Jacobian along field extensions k -> K
targets.note: Base change of abelian varieties and their homomorphisms along a field extension exists, but there is no Jacobian to compare with the Jacobian of the base-changed curve.

duplicates.note: States Jacobians and Abel-Jacobi constructions with base-point hypotheses and an extension-of-scalars check, routed through JacobianChallenge.

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/StableReduction.summary: Tau Ceti has made a start on two layers: Layer 0 has generic and special fibres over a DVR (open and closed immersions, the comparison with the scheme-theoretic fibre at the generic point, scalar-extension towers), the FiniteDVRExtension package with its category of compatible maps, and flat finitely presented models with generic-fibre identification, morphisms, isomorphisms and a separate properness predicate; Layer 6 has the abstract theory of numerical types (Stacks 0C6Z) with the no-cut connectedness criterion, equivalences, the integer signed genus, the weighted Picard group Pic(T) with its injection into Coker(A), rank one, prime torsion, minimality and the first boundedness estimates (0C7B, 0C9U, 0C9V). Mathlib contributes only general ingredients (valuative criteria, Proj of a graded ring, relative normalization, Kähler differentials and the smooth locus, regular local rings, the ring-level Rees algebra, fpqc descent of morphisms). Genuinely missing are fibrewise relative dimension, common refinements of DVR extensions and base change of models, Fitting ideals and the sheaf of differentials, syntomic and nodal morphisms, dual graphs, coherent pushforward with cohomology and base change, arithmetic genus in families, dualizing sheaves, ampleness and relative Proj, polarized and contraction descent, prestable, stable and pointed curves with clutching and contractions, blowups and intersection theory on arithmetic surfaces, regular and minimal models, the geometric side of numerical types with the ℓ-torsion and 768g bounds, semistable and stable reduction in every genus, and stable maps with their whole API.

targets.target: Operations on quasi-coherent / finitely presented O_X-modules needed to construct Omega_{X/S}, Fitting ideals, conductors and normalization exact sequences, with pullback compatibility (Mathlib #39989)
targets.note: The predicates, tilde/affine-presentation API and pullback/pushforward functors of O_X-modules are in Mathlib, Tau Ceti packages finitely presented sheaves as a full subcategory, Mathlib has a presheaf-level universal derivation for a morphism of presheaves of rings (identity-functor case only) and the ring-theoretic conductor of R<x> in S. Missing: Omega_{X/S} as a quasi-coherent sheaf on schemes, Fitting ideals (absent from both libraries), the conductor ideal sheaf, normalization exact sequences, and preservation of quasi-coherence/finite presentation under pullback (only pushforward, open restriction and pullback of free sheaves are covered at this pin).

targets.target: Relative dimension <= d and pure relative dimension d for locally finite type morphisms, defined fibrewise via Krull dimension; isomorphism invariance, locality, arbitrary base change, composition bound <= d + e
targets.note: No fibrewise relative-dimension predicate exists; Mathlib only has relative dimension for smooth morphisms (SmoothOfRelativeDimension, with base change and composition) plus scheme-theoretic fibres and topological Krull dimension. Tau Ceti proves the affine input that dim(K tensor_k A) = dim A for a finitely generated k-algebra A and a field extension K/k, but nothing at scheme level.

targets.target: FamilyOfCurves f: proper, flat, finitely presented, relative dimension <= 1, with base-change and isomorphism API (geometric connectedness and genus kept separate)
targets.note: The constituent morphism properties and their base-change stability are in Mathlib, but the predicate is absent in both libraries because the relative-dimension bound is absent.

targets.target: Generic and special fibres over a DVR: open immersion of the generic fibre, closed immersion of the special fibre, compatibility with scalar extension, and explicit comparison of the base-change generic fibre with Scheme.Hom.fiber at the generic point via kappa(eta) = K

No separate lemma is stated for special fibres after a DVR extension, but that follows from the general tower isomorphism.

targets.target: FiniteDVRExtension R K package (finite separable K'/K, integral closure, chosen maximal ideal above the closed point, localization, fraction-field identification, domination), finite and separable towers, and common-refinement lemmas embedding two packages compatibly into a third

Missing: common refinement; Tower.lean explicitly says the existence of a third package receiving two given ones compatibly is not asserted.

targets.target: Flat finitely presented models of C/K over R with explicit generic-fibre isomorphism: model morphisms, category instance, categorical model isomorphisms, base-change functors, separate properness predicate

targets.target: Kähler differentials and Fitting ideals developed far enough to form the relative singular closed subscheme Sing(f)

targets.target: Syntomic morphisms (flat, locally finitely presented local complete intersections) and their relative-dimension API

targets.note: Absent. The only node-specific material is Tau Ceti's coordinate-level tangent quadratic of a singular Weierstrass cubic; Mathlib's étale-local structure theorem covers standard smooth algebras, not nodes.

targets.target: Relative dualizing complex/sheaf for proper flat finitely presented relative Cohen–Macaulay curves; invertibility and arbitrary base change for Gorenstein fibres; nodal case via a syntomic morphism through a smooth embedding (Stacks 0E6N); agreement with the Jacobian roadmap's omega_{X/k}

targets.target: Invertible-sheaf API (tensor powers, Cartier divisors, pullback, degree on components, global generation, relative ampleness), projective morphisms and relative Proj of a finitely generated graded quasi-coherent algebra connected to Mathlib's Proj, and proper models by scheme-theoretic closure in P^N_R

targets.target: Ampleness criterion on a proper curve by positive degree on every geometric irreducible component; explicit degree bounds and global generation of omega^m and omega(sum s_i)^m
targets.note: Absent: no ampleness, global generation, degree of invertible sheaves or dualizing sheaf in either library.

targets.note: Absent; only the ingredient that universally closed morphisms are closed maps is available.

States effective fpqc/fppf descent for the required objects, overlapping Layer 2's effective descent of polarized schemes.

States that a section of a separated smooth relative curve defines a relative effective Cartier divisor and that sums and arbitrary base change preserve them, overlapping Layer 2's section/effective Cartier divisor target (smooth curves only).

States effective faithfully flat descent of projective relative curves with a compatibly descended relatively ample line bundle, plus sections and morphisms, overlapping Layer 2's polarized descent target.

targets.target: Prestable families (proper, at-worst-nodal, pure relative dimension one, geometrically connected fibres), equivalence with universal f_* O_X = O_S, restriction, pullback and fibre API
targets.note: Absent; only geometric connectedness of morphisms (Mathlib) is available as an ingredient.

targets.target: SemistableFamily and StableFamily with genus bounds; semistable iff no rational tails iff fibrewise global generation of omega^m (m >= 2); stable iff no rational tails or bridges iff omega relatively ample
targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.note: Absent; only Proj of a single graded ring exists (no relative Proj, Veronese invariance, or cohomology and base change).

targets.note: Absent from both libraries.

targets.target: Negative-semidefinite intersection matrix of the special-fibre components, with kernel spanned by the fibre
targets.note: The geometric statement is absent. The inequality x^T A x <= 0 is not proved.

targets.target: Exceptional curves of the first kind and the curve-on-surface (Castelnuovo) contraction theorem, preserving properness and the generic fibre

Plans arithmetic-surface resolution, local charts, vertical components and intersection multiplicities on a regular proper model of an elliptic curve, overlapping the resolution and intersection-multiplicity targets.

Plans finite-place intersection lengths on regular models of curves, vertical divisors, intersection matrices and their kernel, and projection formulas, overlapping this layer's intersection-theory target.
Lists flattening by blowup and strict transforms among its own tasks, overlapping the blowup and strict-transform target.

targets.target: Regular proper model of a smooth projective curve over a DVR, constructed from Layer 4

Neither library defines regular schemes or models (Mathlib has only regular local rings and regular rings), and none is constructed.

targets.target: Components and multiplicities of the special fibre: div_X(pi) = sum m_i [C_i], and the effective Cartier subscheme cut out by pi equals X_s

targets.target: Intersection relations for the special-fibre components, adjunction and the genus formula
targets.note: Needs the Layer 4 intersection theory and relative dualizing sheaves, which do not exist.

Lists regular models of curves over number fields with their vertical divisors among its own constructions, overlapping the regular-model and special-fibre component targets.

targets.target: Abstract numerical type exactly as in Stacks 0C6Z (nonempty finite component set, m_i, w_i > 0, g_i >= 0, symmetric A with nonnegative off-diagonal entries, connected graph, sum_j a_ij m_j = 0, w_i | a_ij)

Basic consequences such as a_ii < 0 when n > 1 (0C74) are proved.

targets.target: Equivalence of graph connectedness with the source's no-disconnected-cut condition
targets.note: The matrix lemma is an iff for any matrix with nonnegative off-diagonal entries over a partial order (no symmetry needed). It discharges the connected field from the Stacks cut condition; the numerical-type lemma gives the converse direction in Adj form.

targets.target: Reindexing and equivalence of numerical types
targets.note: Reindexing is along any equivalence of component types, with reindex_refl and reindex_reindex. Equiv (Stacks 0C70) has refl, symm and trans with groupoid laws, and types are equivalent exactly when one is a reindexing of the other. Genus, minimality, Pic and torsion are all shown invariant.

targets.target: Signed genus g(T) = 1 + sum m_i (w_i (g_i - 1) - a_ii/2) as an integer, with sum m_i a_ii even and the halving done once
targets.note: The value is in Z, not truncated to N, and the halving is applied once to the whole sum (Stacks 0C71/0C72). The file checks g(T) = 3 for the README's weighted example, g(T) = -1 for its genus-zero variant, and a type with odd diagonal entries.

targets.target: Numerical type of a regular model (kappa_i = H^0(C_i, O), w_i = [kappa_i : k], g_i = dim H^1(C_i, O)) and identification of g(T) with the generic-fibre genus
targets.note: Only the abstract combinatorial structure exists; nothing constructs a numerical type from a regular model or compares its genus with the generic fibre. This needs Layers 4-5 and coherent cohomology.

targets.target: Pic(T) as the cokernel of e_i -> sum_j (a_ij / w_j) e_j with exact integer division (Stacks 0C7H)
targets.note: Pic(T) is the quotient of Z^Component by the span of the rows of A' = (a_ij / w_j); exactness of the division comes from symmetry plus the row divisibility axiom. A total-degree map Pic(T) -> Z is also provided.

targets.target: Injection Pic(T) -> Coker(A) induced by e_j -> w_j e_j, not an equality (Stacks 0CE7)
targets.note: Injectivity is proved, and surjectivity holds exactly when every weight is 1. The README's worked computation for its example (Pic(T) = Z against the raw cokernel Z + Z/2, and the w = (1,2) case) is not checked in Lean.

targets.target: Rank-one finite generation of Pic(T), reindexing invariance, and prime torsion
targets.note: finrank_Z Pic(T) = 1 (Stacks 0C7I), with finite generation inherited from Z^n as an instance. Pic(T)[l] is a finite ZMod l-module of cardinality l^dim for prime l. Equivalences induce isomorphisms of Pic and of l-torsion, preserving degree, dimension and cardinality.

targets.target: Combinatorial bounds relating Pic(T)[l], the first Betti number g_top of the graph, geometric genera of components and the genus (Stacks 0C6X, 0C7C, 0C9X and the Section 55.17 inequalities)
targets.note: Present: g_top = 1 - n + e, g_top >= 0 (0C78) and the tree criterion. Missing: g >= g_top for minimal types with n > 1 (0C7C), dim Coker(A)[l] <= g_top for l coprime to all a_ij and m_i (0C6X), dim Pic(T)[l] <= g (and <= g_top for minimal T) for l > 768g (0C9X), and every inequality involving geometric genera of components.

targets.target: Classification and boundedness results for minimal numerical types used by the Artin-Winters argument (Stacks Sections 55.5-55.7)
targets.note: Present: (-1)- and (-2)-indices with the sign of genus contributions (0C75, 0C7D), g >= 1 for minimal types with n > 1 (0C7B), the neighbour bounds of 0C9U, and all four bounds of 0C9V (also genus_lt_arithmeticGenus and multiplicity_mul_abs_intersection_self_le), proved without the g >= 2 hypothesis. Missing: m_i |a_ij| <= 768g (0C9W), the classification of proper (-2)-subgraphs (55.5), the minimal types of genus 0 and 1 (0C8S, 0C8T), contraction of a (-1)-index (0C77) with its Picard map (0C7J), and Pic(T) = Z for g <= 0 (0C7K).

targets.target: Comparison of line bundles on the regular model, generic fibre, special fibre, reduced special fibre and numerical type; specialization maps and exact sequences injecting generic l-torsion into Pic of the reduced special fibre (Stacks Section 55.13)
targets.note: Only the numerical side exists (multidegrees, Pic(T), total degree, torsion). There are no models, no Picard groups of special fibres and no specialization maps.

targets.target: For a smooth projective genus-g curve and prime l != char k: a finite separable K'/K with a K'-rational point and Pic(C_K')[l] = (Z/l)^(2g), with the explicit degree bound

Mathlib only supplies Proj of a graded ring and the morphism X → Proj A induced by a ring map A → Γ(X, 𝒪_X) under which the irrelevant ideal generates the unit ideal.

targets.target: Stabilization of a prestable genus ≥ 2 family over a locally Noetherian base: étale-locally add disjoint auxiliary smooth sections making the source pointed-stable (separable smooth points on each geometric component, étale-local lifting, openness of pointed stability), then forget them one at a time with the Layer 3 single-marking contraction; termination by marking count, with geometric fibres the iterated tail-and-bridge contraction
targets.note: No prestable or pointed-stable families, no result producing étale-local sections of a smooth morphism through prescribed points, no openness of pointed stability and no single-marking contraction exist. Mathlib has only the open smooth locus of a locally finitely presented morphism.

targets.target: Uniqueness among contractions with the prescribed geometric fibres (universal c_*𝒪 = 𝒪 plus contraction descent), independence of the auxiliary sections and their order, cocycle condition on overlaps, and polarized étale descent to C → Cˢᵗ → S; the descended family is proper, flat, finitely presented and stable, and the universal c_*𝒪 and R¹c_*𝒪 statements survive descent
targets.note: Mathlib proves the fpqc and fppf topologies on schemes are subcanonical, so morphisms descend along such covers, but neither library has effective descent of (polarized) schemes, relative Proj, higher direct images R¹c_* or a contraction-descent theorem.

targets.target: Stabilization is the identity on already stable fibres and commutes coherently with arbitrary base change; for a tail-free family it is the relative Proj of the pluricanonical algebra, after proving relative generation and base change
targets.note: Only the absolute construction Proj A → Spec A₀ of a graded ring exists (Mathlib). There is no relative Proj of a quasi-coherent graded algebra, no pluricanonical algebra and no stabilization to compare with.

targets.target: Classical stable-reduction existence theorem: a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus ≥ 2 over K acquires a stable model over the local ring of a chosen place of a finite separable extension, via semistable reduction followed by stabilization
targets.note: Tau Ceti has only the Layer 0 packaging: finite separable DVR extensions with a chosen place (whose local ring is proved to be a DVR dominating R) and flat finitely presented models with an explicit generic-fibre identification. There is no semistable reduction, stable family or existence theorem.

targets.target: Uniqueness of stable models over a fixed DVR: the generic-fibre identification extends, through a common regular model and the canonical stabilization, to a unique isomorphism of models
targets.note: Tau Ceti defines model morphisms that respect the generic-fibre identification and proves that model isomorphisms are exactly the morphisms that are isomorphisms on total spaces. Regular models, stabilization and the uniqueness theorem are absent.

targets.target: Stable-reduction interface packaging existence after a finite DVR extension, uniqueness over a fixed DVR and compatibility after a common finite extension
targets.note: Chosen finite DVR extensions form a category and every finite separable extension underlies such a package, but the Tau Ceti file explicitly does not construct common refinements, and there is no stable-reduction statement to package.

targets.target: Extend the generic markings to sections of a proper model by properness, then use finite base change and blowups to make their closures pairwise disjoint and contained in the smooth locus, tracking the generic-fibre identifications
targets.note: Mathlib's valuative criteria (existence for universally closed morphisms, uniqueness for separated ones, over any valuation ring) extend each K-point of the generic fibre of a proper model to a unique section over the DVR; Tau Ceti records the pullback square of a model's chosen generic fibre. Missing: blowups (absent in both libraries) and the finite-base-change and blowup procedure making the extended sections disjoint and smooth, with the generic-fibre bookkeeping for markings.

targets.target: Pointed stabilization of a pointed prestable family with 2g − 2 + n > 0 by the auxiliary-section construction (original markings retained, descent by the final ample log-dualizing sheaf), and the geometric-fibre algorithm (delete an unmarked tail, move the marking of a one-marked tail to its attachment point, replace an unmarked bridge by a node) with termination, order independence and disjoint smooth remaining markings
targets.note: Neither library has marked or pointed curve families, a log-dualizing sheaf, dual graphs with special flags, or any contraction or stabilization construction.

targets.target: Graded log-canonical algebra with multiplication and base-change maps for each nef single-marking step and identification of its Proj with that step's contraction; the composite preserves an already stable marked generic fibre, is unique with the fibrewise contraction property and commutes coherently with base change
targets.note: Mathlib has Proj of a graded ring and its functoriality along graded ring maps, but there are no section algebras of line bundles on schemes, no relative Proj and no dualizing sheaf in either library.

targets.target: Stable pointed reduction for smooth generic curves whenever 2g − 2 + n > 0, including (g, n) = (0, n ≥ 3) and (1, n ≥ 1), after a finite separable extension, together with uniqueness over the fixed DVR
targets.note: Only the Layer 0 packaging of chosen finite DVR extensions and of models with generic-fibre identifications exists (Tau Ceti); there are no pointed stable families and no reduction theorem.

targets.target: Extension to an already stable pointed nodal generic fibre: split and label nodes, branches and components after a finite separable extension, normalize, treat paired branches as markings, apply the pointed theorem componentwise after a common extension and glue by clutching; the glued family is nodal, stable and independent of choices
targets.note: Mathlib has the relative normalization of a qcqs morphism with its universal property, but neither library has nodes, branch labelling, scheme pushouts along sections (clutching) or pointed stable reduction.

targets.target: Forgetting a marking followed by pointed stabilization, with compatibility with base change and coherence of repeated forgetting
targets.note: Absent in both libraries: there are no marked families, forgetful maps or stabilization.

targets.target: Valuative interface: essential existence after a finite DVR extension and unique extension over a fixed DVR, stated as the input for properness of M̄_{g,n} and of stable-map moduli
targets.note: Mathlib's valuative criterion is about morphisms of schemes and arbitrary valuation rings (its reduction to DVRs over a Noetherian base is listed as future work), and Tau Ceti has the finite DVR extension package; the stable-curve valuative statement itself is absent.

duplicates.note: Its internal proof task 2 (de Jong's curve fibrations) states extension of the generic curve and its marked boundary after finite base extension and stable/semistable reduction of that pointed family, to be proved there unless a stable-curve supplier with matching hypotheses exists, overlapping the pointed stable-reduction targets here.

Its contraction of Néron polygons for generalised elliptic curves is the genus-one special case of contracting rational components without markings, i.e. of the pointed stabilization constructed here.

targets.target: PrestableMap q n for a target q : V → S: a pointed prestable family π : C → S with n ordered markings and F : C → V with F ≫ q = π, projections to the source family, and pullback along S' → S through chosen pullbacks, independent of the choices up to canonical isomorphism
targets.note: Neither library has prestable or pointed curve families or any stable-map structure; only general category theory, such as uniqueness of pullbacks up to canonical isomorphism, is available.

targets.target: Isomorphisms of prestable maps over a fixed target (isomorphisms of pointed source curves commuting with F): identity, inverse, composition, extensionality, and transport along isomorphisms of base and target
targets.note: Only generic isomorphisms in over-categories exist (Mathlib); there is no groupoid of prestable maps.

targets.target: Abstract automorphism group of each geometric fibre for a separated locally finitely presented target, and infinitesimal automorphisms over an algebraically closed k (automorphisms over k[ε]/(ε²) reducing to the identity, fixing the markings and commuting with F), with the tangent space identified with the kernel of Der_k(𝒪_C) vanishing along the markings → Der(F⁻¹𝒪_V, 𝒪_C)
targets.note: The available ingredients are general or ring-level: automorphism groups of objects of a category (Mathlib), derivations as lifts to square-zero extensions (Mathlib) and to dual numbers (Tau Ceti). Neither library has derivation sheaves on schemes, automorphism groups of marked curves or maps, or the infinitesimal-automorphism computation.

targets.target: Contracted irreducible components of a geometric fibre: relate constancy of F on the component, set-theoretic image of dimension zero and, for a target with an ample invertible sheaf, degree zero of its pullback; invariance under field extension and target isomorphism
targets.note: Mathlib provides scheme-theoretic fibres and a closed-subscheme structure on irreducible components of Noetherian schemes, but neither library defines contracted components, ample sheaves or degrees of line bundles on curves.

targets.target: IsStableMap F: fibrewise positivity of the log-canonical degree (normalization genus and special flags) on every contracted geometric component; invariance under isomorphism and arbitrary base change; openness over a locally Noetherian base for projective targets with relatively ample L, via fibrewise ampleness of ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) ⊗ F^*(L^⊗3)
targets.note: No stability predicate, dualizing sheaf, ampleness notion or openness-of-ampleness theorem exists in either library.

targets.target: Automorphism criterion for separated locally finitely presented targets: F is stable iff every geometric fibre has finite automorphism group; infinitesimal automorphisms vanish under componentwise generic separability of the noncontracted components
targets.note: Absent in both libraries: there are no automorphism groups of pointed curves or maps and no finiteness or unramifiedness criterion.

targets.target: Ampleness criterion for a projective target with relatively ample L: stability iff relative ampleness of ω_{C/S}(Σsᵢ) ⊗ F^*(L^⊗3), independence of L, and the same for every exponent ≥ 3
targets.note: Mathlib has the pullback functor on sheaves of modules over schemes and Tau Ceti defines invertible sheaves with tensor products, but there are no tensor powers, relative dualizing sheaf, relative ampleness or projective morphisms.

targets.target: A constant prestable map is stable iff its pointed source is stable, while a nonconstant map can be stable with unstable source (an API theorem, not a field of PrestableMap)
targets.note: Absent: neither stable pointed curves nor stable maps are defined in either library.

targets.target: Evaluation morphism evᵢ = sᵢ ≫ F : S → V at the i-th marking, compatible with base change, reindexing of markings, isomorphisms of stable maps and postcomposition on the target
targets.note: Absent: neither library has stable maps or marked families, hence no evaluation morphisms.

targets.target: Polarization degree of a map and of each geometric irreducible component, deg F^*L: nonnegativity, additivity over the components of a nodal curve, invariance under algebraically closed field extension, and local constancy of total degree in connected families
targets.note: Neither library defines the degree of an invertible sheaf on a proper curve; Tau Ceti has only the residue-degree-weighted degree of scheme Weil divisors, and Mathlib the pullback of sheaves of modules. No component degrees, additivity or constancy statements exist.

targets.target: Decorated dual graph with marking legs and component degrees: genus and total-degree formulas, vertex stability (a degree-zero vertex is stable iff 2g_v − 2 + val(v) + markings(v) > 0, equivalently with + 3d_v for a polarization), valence counting half-edges so loops count twice, restriction to a component, normalization at a node and reconstruction of the numerical data
targets.note: Mathlib's multigraph Graph α β allows loops and parallel edges but has no degree, connectivity or Betti-number API; Tau Ceti's numerical-type topological genus is 1 − #components + #edges of a simple intersection graph, without loops, legs, vertex genera or degrees. No dual graph of a curve exists in either library.

targets.target: Contraction descent for proper surjective contractions of prestable curves with universally connected genus-zero fibres and c_*𝒪_C = 𝒪_{C'}: for separated V → S, a map constant on each contracted subcurve factors uniquely through the contraction, compatibly with base change
targets.note: Neither the general contraction-descent theorem of Layer 2 nor this specialization exists; Mathlib's descent of morphisms is only along fpqc and fppf covers, which contractions are not.

targets.target: Reindexing markings by equivalences and the single-marking contraction for a stable map to a projective target when 2g − 2 + n' + 3d > 0 (Behrend–Manin Prop. 3.10, Lemmas 3.11–3.12): nefness of A = ω_{C/S}(Σ retained sᵢ) ⊗ F^*(L^⊗3) and its zero-degree components, the fibre contraction, descent of F and of the ample A', uniform generation, vanishing and normal generation, the Veronese relative Proj, flatness, nodality, structure-sheaf identities, retained smooth disjoint sections, the excluded numerical types, stability of the result, base change and coherence of repeated forgetting
targets.note: Absent in both libraries, and so are its ingredients: dualizing sheaf, nefness, relative Proj, and cohomology and base change.

targets.target: External gluing of stable maps of types (g₁, I ⊔ {a}, d₁) and (g₂, J ⊔ {b}, d₂) with ev_a = ev_b, and self-gluing of type (g, I ⊔ {a, b}, d) with a ≠ b and ev_a = ev_b: descent of the target map through the pushout, stability, the decorated-graph formula, reindexing by marking-set equivalences and coherent base change
targets.note: Absent: neither library has scheme pushouts identifying sections (clutching), stable maps or decorated dual graphs.

targets.target: Map-aware stabilization of an arbitrary prestable map to a projective target with 2g − 2 + n + 3d > 0: étale-local auxiliary markings forgotten by the single-marking construction; geometric algorithm contracting F-constant rational components with at most two current flags (termination, order independence, agreement with the family construction); polarized descent; universal property, uniqueness, independence of auxiliary markings and of L, coherent base change, identity on stable maps; the excluded degree-zero genus-zero and genus-one types admit no stable map
targets.note: Absent in both libraries.

targets.target: Functoriality of stable maps under target isomorphisms and closed immersions, and a sharp criterion for preservation of stability under a general postcomposition V → W
targets.note: Absent: there are no stable maps to transport in either library.

ArithmeticGaloisDuality.summary: The libraries hold only upstream ingredients: Mathlib's canonical continuous cohomology (defined for any topological coefficient module, with compatible-pair functoriality), abstract spectral sequences, the Mittag–Leffler condition for systems of sets, adic-completion exactness and topological restricted products; and Tau Ceti's explicit degree ≤ 2 continuous cohomology, which already accepts non-discrete coefficients (so compact lattices too) for restriction, inflation, corestriction with cor∘res = index, degree-one inflation–restriction exactness and cup products, together with the internal-Hom dual and its equivariant evaluation pairing. Everything arithmetic that the roadmap plans is genuinely missing from both libraries: the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence, lim¹ and derived inverse limits with the passage to compact p-adic coefficients, G_{F,S} with global finiteness, cohomological dimension and Tate's Euler characteristic, compactly supported cohomology, local invariant maps and local, global and Poitou–Tate duality in finite, compact and lattice forms, Galois-cohomological Selmer groups with the Greenberg–Wiles formula, and all Galois deformation theory and Taylor–Wiles numerics. Several layers restate targets that other roadmaps also state (ProfiniteCohomology, ClassFieldTheory, SelmerIwasawaCohomology, GlobalGaloisDeformations, CompletedCohomologyPartII, DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra).

targets.target: Localization morphism of continuous cochain complexes C•(G_{F,S},T) → ⊕_{v∈S} C•(G_{F_v},T) and the compact-support fibre
targets.note: Mathlib supplies compatible-pair cochain maps, mapping cones and the map of absolute Galois groups for a field extension, but G_{F,S}, the localisation morphism and the compact-support fibre are not constructed.

targets.target: Topological restricted products, unramified subgroups and their transition maps, with the topology in each finite/compact/discrete coefficient regime
targets.note: Mathlib has restricted products with their topology and continuous functoriality along compatible maps; missing are unramified cohomology subgroups, their transition maps and the coefficient-regime topologies.

targets.target: Derived-limit comparisons retaining lim¹ until a proved Mittag–Leffler condition eliminates it
targets.note: Only the Mittag–Leffler condition for set-valued cofiltered systems exists (Mathlib); there is no Rlim/lim¹ for abelian groups or complexes and no comparison for continuous cochains.

targets.target: Continuous Hochschild–Serre with convergence hypotheses, five-term/edge maps and agreement with the discrete upstream construction
targets.note: Only the first nodes of the five-term sequence exist (degree-1 inflation–restriction exactness in Tau Ceti) plus abstract spectral sequences in Mathlib; the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence, convergence, transgression and remaining edge-map exactness are missing.

targets.target: One reciprocity/sign normalization shared by restriction, corestriction, cup products, Shapiro and local invariant maps
targets.note: Tau Ceti fixes and proves the low-degree compatibilities (projection formula, restriction of cups, graded commutativity, cor∘δ = δ∘cor) and Shapiro in degrees 0–1; missing are local invariant maps, all-degree cups/corestriction/Shapiro and their mutual compatibilities.

targets.target: Derived local and global duality via the derived O-linear or Pontryagin dual and Tate twist, retaining modified Tate terms at real places when p = 2
targets.note: Only ingredients exist: the Pontryagin dual of a topological group and the p-adic cyclotomic character (Mathlib), and the finite internal-hom dual with evaluation pairing (Tau Ceti); no local or global duality theorem in any form.

targets.target: Finite, compact and discrete-torsion formulations of duality, with the inverse-limit and continuous-dual hypotheses used to pass between them
targets.note: Absent in both libraries.

targets.target: Perfectness/amplitude of globally compactly supported versus local-condition complexes under finite-generation hypotheses
targets.note: Absent; no arithmetic cochain complexes with perfectness statements exist.

targets.target: Recovery of the finite nine-term sequence and the lattice/rational sequences with topological-closure and derived-limit terms
targets.note: Absent in both libraries.

duplicates.note: Also plans derived inverse limits of complexes, the Milnor lim¹ sequence and Mittag–Leffler criteria, overlapping D7's derived-limit comparisons.
Also states constructing a continuous Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence with edge maps, although it cites D7 as supplier.
Also plans derived Mittag–Leffler comparisons with retained lim¹ and perfectness/Tor-amplitude of complexes, overlapping D7's derived-limit and perfectness/amplitude targets.
Owns local Tate duality for finite modules and the normalized local invariant, which D7's finite formulation of derived local duality and its invariant-map normalization would restate.

targets.target: Comparison of H¹ of the imported Selmer complex (shifted cone of global plus local-condition cochains) with R02.5's deformation Selmer kernel, retaining H⁰ corrections
targets.note: Absent; neither library has Selmer complexes or Galois-cohomological Selmer groups.

targets.target: Transport of D7 duality along the Selmer-complex triangle
targets.note: Absent; no duality theorem exists to transport.

targets.target: Dual Selmer dimension calculation in all ranks, including the trace-kernel exceptions when p divides n
targets.note: Absent in both libraries.

targets.target: Determinant/deformation tangent complexes built from the actual restriction maps
targets.note: Only End(V) as a representation by conjugation exists (Mathlib); no deformation tangent complexes or Galois deformation theory.

targets.target: Change-of-coefficients spectral sequence with Tor terms; underived specialization only after the Tor terms vanish
targets.note: Mathlib defines Tor in monoidal abelian categories via left derived functors and abstract spectral sequences, but no base-change (Tor) spectral sequence for complexes and no specialization of Galois cochain complexes.

duplicates.note: Also proves that the Selmer mapping-fibre complex recovers the classical Selmer group under H⁰ conditions, the comparison D8 states.

Also proves the tangent and obstruction spaces of polarized dimension-n problems, the failure of scalar/traceless splitting when p divides n, and dual-Selmer control, overlapping D8's tangent-complex and dual-Selmer targets.
Also proves the spectral sequence Tor_i^A(H^j(C),B) ⇒ H^{j−i}(C ⊗^L_A B), which is D8's change-of-coefficients spectral sequence.
Also proves specialization spectral sequences for Iwasawa cohomology, a change-of-coefficients Tor spectral sequence for Galois complexes.

targets.note: Mathlib's continuousCohomology is defined for every object of TopRep k G, so H^n(G,T), H^n(G,T/ϖ^n) and H^n(G,V) exist as objects, and Tau Ceti's explicit continuous-cochain H¹/H² accept arbitrary topological coefficient groups. targets.note: Mathlib has the Mittag–Leffler condition for cofiltered systems of types (eventual ranges, ML from finite ranges, nonempty limits of finite nonempty systems). targets.target: Separate treatment of T, V = T[1/p] and V/T (rationalization H^i(G,V) = H^i(G,T)⊗Q_p, H^i(G,V/T) as a colimit over ϖ^{-n}T/T, and the sequence attached to 0 → T → V → V/T → 0)

targets.note: Mathlib has only the algebraic adic-completion facts (for finite modules over a Noetherian ring the completion is M ⊗ R̂, R̂ is flat, completion is exact). targets.target: Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence H^p(G/N, H^q(N,M)) ⇒ H^{p+q}(G,M) for a closed normal subgroup N of a profinite group, with topology and convergence conditions

Owns the degree 0–2 restriction/corestriction identities (cor∘res = index, transitivity, Mackey) that R02.2 also asks to prove.
Owns all-degree corestriction with cor∘res, transitivity and the Mackey formula, overlapping R02.2's restriction/corestriction identities.

targets.target: G_{F,S}: Galois group of the maximal extension of a number field F unramified outside a finite set S containing the archimedean places and the places above p
targets.note: Neither library defines a maximal extension unramified outside S or its Galois group; available are the absolute Galois group with the Krull topology, the infinite Galois correspondence, unramifiedness of infinite places, and descent of unramified-outside-S along towers of number fields.

targets.target: Finiteness of H^i(G_{F,S}, M) for finite M of order invertible on S

targets.target: Bounds on the cohomological dimension of G_{F,S} (cd_p ≤ 2 for p odd or F totally imaginary) with the real-place exceptions
targets.note: No cohomological dimension of profinite groups is defined in either library (ProfiniteCohomology Layer 11 is unbuilt), and no bound for any Galois group of a number field.

targets.target: Tate's global Euler-characteristic formula for G_{F,S}
targets.note: Absent; the Euler-characteristic API in Mathlib and Tau Ceti concerns graded objects, finite complexes and Grothendieck groups, not Galois cohomology.

targets.target: Compactly supported arithmetic cohomology as the fibre of the localisation map, with the corrected (Tate) terms at infinite places
targets.note: Only general ingredients exist: mapping cones and the homogeneous continuous cochain complex (Mathlib), Tate cohomology of finite groups (Mathlib) and its 2-periodicity for cyclic groups (Tau Ceti); no localisation morphism or compact-support complex.

targets.target: Identification of the global restriction (localisation) maps H^i(G_{F,S},M) → H^i(G_{F_v},M) with the placewise maps of R01
targets.note: Mathlib gives the continuous homomorphism of absolute Galois groups induced by a field extension such as F → F_v (depending on a chosen embedding of algebraic closures) and compatible-pair functoriality of continuous cohomology, which together would define localisation maps; no localisation map is constructed or compared.

targets.target: Local invariant maps inv_v : H²(G_{F_v}, μ) → Q/Z, including real places, and the reciprocity Σ_v inv_v = 0
targets.note: No cohomological Brauer group or invariant map exists (ClassFieldTheory Layers 5 and 10 are unbuilt); Tau Ceti has only the central-simple-algebra Brauer group with base change and Br(ℝ) ≅ ℤ/2.

targets.target: Restricted product of local cohomology groups with respect to unramified classes, with its topology
targets.note: Mathlib has restricted products with their topology and topological-group structure; missing are the unramified subgroups H^i_nr(G_{F_v},M) and the restricted product of local cohomology groups built from them.

targets.target: Poitou–Tate global duality: perfect pairing Ш¹_S(M) × Ш²_S(M^∨(1)) → Q/Z, including global duality itself
targets.note: Absent: there are no Tate–Shafarevich groups of Galois modules, no global pairing and no local Tate duality (ClassFieldTheory Layer 5 is unbuilt).

targets.target: Nine-term Poitou–Tate exact sequence for finite modules
targets.note: Absent in both libraries.

targets.target: Lattice and rational-coefficient versions of the duality and exact sequence, with the limit arguments recorded
targets.note: Absent; no inverse-limit or lim¹ theory for Galois cohomology exists to pass from finite to compact coefficients.
